items.front: Eastern Satavahana capital in coastal Andhra (Krishna valley)?
items.back: Dhanyakataka / Dharanikota (near Amaravati) — the Andhra power centre of the Puranic 'Andhras'.

items.front: The Amaravati Mahachaitya — where is it and who patronised it?
items.back: Palnadu district; patronised by Satavahanas & Ikshvakus (c.3rd BCE–250 CE); ayaka pillars; ASI-protected.

items.front: Medium and hallmark of the Amaravati school of art?
items.back: White/greenish limestone; narrative Buddhist reliefs; early aniconic 'empty throne'; influenced Sri Lanka & SE Asia.

items.front: Bhattiprolu (Guntur/Bapatla) is famous for what two things?
items.back: Buddha relic caskets, and the early southern 'Bhattiprolu' script (a Brahmi variant).

items.front: Who succeeded the Satavahanas in the lower Krishna valley, and their capital?
items.back: The Ikshvakus of Vijayapuri (Nagarjunakonda), c.3rd–4th c CE.

items.front: Founder of the Andhra Ikshvaku dynasty?
Ikshvaku king under whom Buddhism flourished; whose sister built the Mahachaitya?
items.back: Virapurushadatta; his sister/aunt Chamtisiri (Shantisri) endowed the Nagarjunakonda Mahachaitya.

items.front: Religious duality of the Ikshvaku court?
items.back: Kings performed Vedic sacrifices (ashvamedha/vajapeya) while royal women patronised Buddhism.

items.front: Nagarjunakonda's original name, and why was it relocated?
items.back: Vijayapuri; the valley was submerged by the Nagarjuna Sagar dam, so monuments were shifted to an island museum.

items.front: Acharya Nagarjuna's philosophy and chief text?
Kalinga Buddhist site on the Vamsadhara in Srikakulam?
items.back: Salihundam — with Hinayana, Mahayana and Vajrayana phases.

items.front: Salankayanas of Vengi — capital and emblem?
items.back: Capital Vengi/Pedavegi (Godavari–Krishna doab), c.300–440 CE; bull emblem.

items.front: Greatest Vishnukundin king, and who ended the dynasty?
items.back: Madhava Varma (performed ashvamedha); ended by Pulakeshin II, paving the way for the Eastern Chalukyas.
